title: More than a defense: salicylic acid's secret role in fruit color
content: The vibrant red skin of an apple (Malus domestica) is not only a visual delight for consumers but also an important biological trait. The variation in the color of different apple varieties comes from varying proportions of a flavonoid pigment, anthocyanin, in the apple fruit skin. Anthocyanin not only provides coloration but also serves to attract seed dispersers and protect the fruit from the UV radiation and fluctuating temperatures (Steyn et al. 2002; Shang et al. 2011; Zhao et al. 2023). Although the role of ripening hormones such as ethylene and abscisic acid is well documented in promoting pigmentation in fruits, the influence of defense-related hormones in fruit pigmentation has remained less explored.
